episodes.198884: Three days of heavy rain from a slow moving frontal system caused the Coquille River at Coquille to briefly and slightly rise above minor flood stage.
episodes.198885: Three days of heavy rain from a slow moving frontal system and snow melt caused the Sprague River near Beatty to rise above minor flood stage.
episodes.198890: Thunderstorms associated with a sharp shortwave trough moving across the eastern Gulf and attendant surface low pressure system produce gusty marine winds from Charlotte Harbor and Pine Island Sound to areas around San Carlos Bay and the mouth of the Caloosahatchee River.
episodes.199795: A strengthening upper-level low and an associated strong low pressure system at the surface tracked just off the Pacific Northwest coast leading to a period of high winds. Warmer temperatures, additional rainfall and prior snowfall to this event facilitated localized flooding as well. The frontal passage during the early afternoon hours of Feb 24th allowed for a period of isolated severe thunderstorms later that afternoon due to a low CAPE but high shear environment.
episodes.199796: A strengthening upper-level low and an associated strong low pressure system at the surface tracked just off the Pacific Northwest coast leading to a period of high winds. Heavy snow also fell across the south Washington Cascades during this period in addition to localized flooding on the Grays River near the coast. The frontal passage during the early afternoon hours of Feb 24th allowed for a period of isolated severe thunderstorms later that afternoon due to a low CAPE but high shear environment.

Grays River at Covered Bridge near Rosburg. Reached minor flood stage (28.5 ft) 2/25 at 3 15 am. Reached Moderate Flood (30.5 ft) 2/25 at 645 am. Peaked at 31.9 feet 2/25 at 1215pm. Fell below Moderate 2/25 at 2030 PST. Fell below minor at 2/26 5 am.

The Sprague River near Beatty rose above minor flood stage of 8.5 ft. at 25/730 PST, peaked in minor flood stage at 26/145 PST at 9.13 ft. It then fell below flood stage at 26/1645 PST. This produced flooding of structures in the vicinity of the cities of Sprague River and Lone Pine, and widespread agricultural flooding.
The Coquille River at Coquille rose above minor flood stage of 21.0 ft. at 25/1115 PST, peaked in minor flood stage at 25/1215 PST at 21.04 ft. It then fell below flood stage at 25/1430 PST.
